title: tool-call choreography: deterministic result injection and retry bounding
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds deterministic tool-call choreography with bounded retries and improved OpenAI-compatible function_call mapping. Improves streaming stability for tool-heavy prompts and introduces opt-in idempotency tokens for multi-tool sequences.
description: Context: we see intermittent nondeterminism and duplicated tool side-effects in multi-tool/high-parallel prompts (customer-reported via SUP-908). Motivation: make tool-calling behavior predictable for application developers while keeping throughput and streaming responsiveness. This PR implements a lightweight choreography layer that: 1) assigns a deterministic execution order to tool calls by default when a prompt declares 'composed_tools' intent; 2) injects tool results deterministically into the response context (no racey KV cache races); 3) bounds retry budgets per-tool-call (configurable) and surfaces retry reasons to the API user; 4) adds an opt-in idempotency token in the OpenAI-compatible function_call flow so external tools can dedupe side-effects. Changes are backward-compatible for simple single-tool function_call usage but opt into choreography semantics when the request includes the new header or field (x-redwood-tool-choreography: ordered|parallel). This PR also tightens streaming stability when tool results are being fetched by holding the final chunk stream open until injection completes, then resuming a steady streaming session (reduces truncated JSON errors seen with nested tool calls). Checklist: - [x] design doc (ENG-4412) reviewed - [x] unit tests for choreography scheduler - [x] integration tests with python/ts SDK examples - [x] manual smoke tests on Dedicated pool - [x] docs draft for API and migration notes (redwood-docs PR pending) Linked work: ENG-4412 (design), ENG-4487 (retry budgeting), SUP-908 (customer case). Rolling plan: feature gated behind request-level header; default remains legacy behavior until GA toggle.

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Overall LGTM, small nit on scheduler backoff constants — prefer using constants/feature flag. Author: adjusted to Config.MAX_CHOREO_BACKOFF and left feature flag gating.

Hannah Li: Can we guarantee no extra stream chunk reordering? Concern about holding stream until tool returns causing head-of-line blocking. Author: added bounded waiting (default 250ms) and fallback to emit placeholder and later patch via delta-streaming; added tests.
Ravi Kaur: Add telemetry for retry_reason and retry_count per tool. Author: added redwood.choreo.retry_reason tag and included in traces.

QA (Maya): Hit a flaky in dedicated canary where one tool call timed out, causing sequencer lock for subsequent requests. Author: adjusted per-request semaphore to be per-session not global and added timeouts; CI re-ran and passed.
Security (Omar): Make sure idempotency token cannot be used to escalate privileges. Author: token is opaque, validated server-side and scoped to call_id; added unit test.

files_summary: Added new choreographer runtime module and scheduler tests
API surface: header/field parsing for choreography, idempotency propagation for OpenAI-compatible function_call
SDKs: convenience flags and streaming backpressure handling in Python/TS
Metrics and CI: new metrics and choreography e2e stage
testing_notes: Local dedicated smoke tests run against a 2-GPU pool with simulated slow tools. Verified: ordered injection produces same final response across 50 runs; parallel mode keeps preexisting behavior and shows 5-8% throughput improvement for purely parallel tool-heavy prompts. Observed median extra streaming latency of ~40ms in ordered mode when waiting for tool injection; configurable lower bound set to 0 for aggressive latency tradeoffs.
notes_for_backport: No immediate backport to 1.4.x — heavy runtime change. If requested, can cherry-pick the API parsing and idempotency mapping only (low risk).
migration_guidance: Default behavior unchanged. To opt in: include header 'x-redwood-tool-choreography: ordered' or set request body field 'tool_choreography: "ordered"'. When enabled, tool calls are executed in deterministic order and tool outputs are injected before final streaming closure. To avoid head-of-line blocking, set 'choreography_wait_ms' in request metadata (default 250). SDKs expose convenience param 'tool_choreography' (python/ts). Testing: run integration e2e against dedicated pool before enabling for production traffic.
impact_assessment: User-visible: new header opt-in only; existing single-tool function_call behavior unaffected. Operational: small additional latency when ordering is requested; adds new metrics for retries and latency. Risk: medium until GA due to runtime semaphores; mitigations: feature-flag, per-request timeouts, telemetry.
final_status_message: Merged after stakeholder approvals and CI green. Feature gated and rolled out to canary customers; docs and SDK PRs will follow for broader adoption.
